clue.text: Thai leader of impetuous nature? Rubbish!

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so take the start of Thai

parts.note: someone of impetuous nature is rash, acting without thinking

explanation.surface: A Thai head of state is called hot-headed, and someone scoffs at the claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish!' looks like a scornful reply to the question, but it is the definition, used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Trash and rubbish are synonyms for worthless waste or nonsense.

clue.text: Awful strain imposed on Conservative in passing

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece imposed on another sits on top of it, so it comes first
awful suggests something messed up, so the letters of strain are scrambled

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A dreadful burden is placed on a Tory politician, mentioned only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' scrambles STRAIN into TRANSI, which 'imposed on' stacks above TORY in this down light; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing lasts only a short while, which is what transitory means: fleeting.

clue.text: To ventilate factory is a bloomer

parts.note: to ventilate a room is to air it
a factory is a plant, an industrial works

explanation.surface: Someone claims that letting fresh air into a factory is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a blunder, but here it is literally something that blooms: an air plant is a flowering epiphyte that grows without soil.
explanation.definitionFit: An air plant is a flowering plant, so it is a bloomer in the literal sense of something that produces blossoms.

clue.text: Workman and I excel, despite disadvantage

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to cap something is to outdo or surpass it

explanation.surface: A labourer and the speaker do brilliantly although they start at a disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'despite' is a link word joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a hindrance or impediment that makes success harder.

clue.text: Was anguished to diagnose disorder

indicators.note: a disorder is a jumble, so the letters of diagnose are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A patient was distressed at having a medical disorder identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' reads as the illness being diagnosed, but it is the anagram signal working on DIAGNOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have agonised is to have suffered great mental torment, which is being anguished.

clue.text: Operatic heroine beside a Cretan mount

parts.note: Mount Ida is the highest mountain on Crete

explanation.surface: An opera's leading lady stands next to a mountain in Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beside' is a link word placing the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is the title heroine of Verdi's opera, an Ethiopian princess enslaved in Egypt.

clue.text: Fancy putting Spanish uncle into negative accommodation!

indicators.note: into says the uncle is placed within the negative word, splitting it open

parts.note: non is a negating prefix meaning not
tio is the Spanish word for uncle

explanation.surface: Someone imagines squeezing a visiting Spanish relative into an unsuitable room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... into' signals the container, the uncle splitting the negative after two letters; 'accommodation' only dresses the surface as a room for the guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is an idea or whim, which is what a notion is.

clue.text: Pay up to get a seat

definitions.meaning: to pay up is to ... a bill or debt
a long wooden bench with a high back

explanation.definitionFit: Settling an account means paying what is owed, and a settle is an old-fashioned high-backed bench.

clue.text: Finished by being taken for a ride

definitions.meaning: being taken for a ride is being cheated or swindled

explanation.definitionFit: Done means completed, and informally to be done is to be conned, as in done out of money.

clue.text: Ordered to find a way round mountain chain

indicators.note: round says the way is wrapped around the mountain chain

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Someone was told to locate a route skirting the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find' is a link; 'round' wraps the abbreviated way around the mountains, and the A goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged means put in order, sorted into a sequence.

clue.text: I shan't be befuddled by strong drink

indicators.note: befuddled means confused, so the letters of I shan't be are muddled

explanation.surface: A drinker vows not to be made tipsy by hard liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'befuddled' reads as drunk, but signals the letters of I SHAN'T BE being rearranged; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a potent green spirit flavoured with wormwood, famously high in alcohol.

clue.text: Blasted man supplying second-rate barge

parts.note: B is a second-class grade, as in B-movie
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for loading ships

explanation.surface: A man is cursed for providing an inferior canal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplying' is a link word. 'Blasted' reads as a curse word, but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighter is a mild British term of abuse for a person, roughly a confounded fellow.

clue.text: Egocentric novice left to market seafood

indicators.note: left means departed, so the novice goes from the word for market

parts.note: to market goods is to sell them
L is the learner plate on a novice driver's car
fish is food from the sea

explanation.surface: A self-centred beginner set out to trade in seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as the past of leave a place; it signals L leaving SELL to give SEL; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone egocentric thinks only of themselves, which is being selfish.

clue.text: Some workers are on it for an interval

definitions.meaning: workers on short time work only part of the week
an interval is a break midway through a match

explanation.definitionFit: Half-time is a reduced working week for some staff, and also the break between the two halves of a game.

clue.text: Lamenting malformation — that's true

definitions.note: true here is the noun, as in out of true

indicators.note: a malformation is a faulty shape, so the letters of lamenting are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone grieves over a deformity, insisting it is genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'true' reads as an adjective meaning correct; here it is the noun of 'out of true', the state of being properly lined up.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is in true it is correctly lined up, so true as a noun means proper positioning.

clue.text: Customs officer, as king Canute was

definitions.meaning: a historical official who boarded ships arriving on the tide to collect duties
the legend has King Canute waiting on the shore for the sea to obey him

explanation.definitionFit: A tidewaiter was a customs official who met incoming ships, and Canute in legend sat awaiting the turning sea.

clue.text: Where astronauts become elated?

definitions.meaning: astronauts in orbit are literally high above the globe

explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts orbit high above our planet, and the idiom for feeling ecstatic says the same.

clue.text: Driver means to travel north in a punt

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the word for the punt

parts.note: a punt is a bet, a wager
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A chauffeur explains how to head upstream in a flat boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a flat river boat, but it is a bet. 'means to' is a link, and 'in' sets the travel-plus-north pair inside the bet after three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A waggoner drives a horse-drawn wagon.

clue.text: Pressure results from two forms of transport

parts.note: rail, travelling by train, is one form of transport
road, travelling by car or lorry, is another

explanation.surface: Stress comes from having to use both trains and cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'results from' is a link phrase; the one phrase gives both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad someone is to force them into acting quickly, to pressure them.

clue.text: Prince Andrew and family rent land in the north

parts.note: Prince Andrew was Duke of York, so he and his daughters are the Yorks
to rent something is to hire it

explanation.surface: Royal relatives lease an estate in northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like a payment; it is the verb to hire.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire is a large historic county of northern England.

clue.text: Cleric hesitates to display lapel

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a title for a clergyman
er is the sound of hesitation, so ers are hesitations

explanation.surface: A vicar dithers before showing off a jacket feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to display' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Revers is the turned-back edge of a coat or jacket, the same as a lapel.

clue.text: Put into space? That's a parody

definitions.meaning: a rocket launch sends a craft aloft
a parody is a mocking imitation

explanation.definitionFit: To send something up is to launch it skyward, and a send-up is a comic spoof.

clue.text: Top-quality beer upset over ceremonial gear

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 read as the letter I
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Fine ale is spilt on a set of ceremonial robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AILAGER round to give REGALIA; 'over' is a link. A1, top-class, appears with its 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the robes and emblems worn on state occasions, such as a crown and sceptre.

clue.text: Are they made by amorous loan sharks?

definitions.text: Are they made by amorous loan sharks?

parts.words: Are they made by amorous loan sharks?
parts.note: moneylenders lend sums of money up front, and amorous people make romantic approaches; the same word covers both

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about lovesick moneylenders.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances are loans paid ahead and also romantic overtures, both of which an amorous moneylender might offer.

clue.text: A love for deep blue

parts.note: love is a score of zero in tennis, which is nil

explanation.surface: Someone declares a passion for dark blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the deep blue dye made from it.

clue.text: Notice an epidermal blemish

definitions.meaning: to notice something is to see or detect it

explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to catch sight of something, and a spot is a pimple on the skin.

clue.text: Show that decimalised figure is incorrect

parts.note: a decimal figure has a point in it
out means wrong, as in your sums are out

explanation.surface: Someone demonstrates that a number written in decimals is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something to someone is to indicate it, draw their attention to it.

clue.text: Final job for an army bugler

definitions.text: Final job for an army bugler

parts.note: final means last
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: The last task of an army bugler's day.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the Last Post is the bugle call sounded at the end of the day and at military funerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Post is a bugle call played in the British army at nightfall and at remembrance ceremonies.

clue.text: Appendage needed by a cyclist

definitions.meaning: an extra clause added to a document or bill

explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an added clause attached to a contract, and anyone on a bike is a rider.
